chunks: And the Imam (peace be upon him) said:
"Whoever says, when he prays Maghrib, three times: 'All praise is for Allah, who does what He wills, and none other than Him does what He wills,' will be given abundant good."
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting this specific dhikr after Maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes this specific dhikr for recitation after Maghrib, highlighting the theological principle of divine sovereignty where all action originates solely from Allah. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on post-prayer supplications as a means to accumulate spiritual merit, linking the believer's gratitude directly to Allah's exclusive will (*mashiya*) and power (*qudrah*).
